brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base is the build.
requirements.evidence: One piece: hex base, half-n variant, at q0 r0 level0. No other base placed.

Only one drawer can be placed on a half base: its single cut face offers one drawer (key 's'). After adding it, no further drawer offers exist on this base, and a second key ('t') is refused. Five drawers on one base is not reachable in this configurator. Built: 1 drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut).

requirements.requirement: Nothing else is added beside or on top of the base (no other parts, covers, bins, accessories or props).
requirements.evidence: Build contains only the half base and its one drawer; no covers, caps, bins, props or other cells. check_build: meshClash clear, only an info note about open cap faces (no cap added, as the brief forbids extras).

finish.summary: The build is one half hex base (half-n) with one drawer. The brief asked for five drawers on that single base, but the configurator offers only one drawer per half base (one cut face, one key), so five cannot be placed on a single base. The requirement is unmet; nothing else was added. Five drawers would need either five drawer-bearing bases, which breaks the single-base requirement, or a different approach the configurator does not offer.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
